subject: Trouble warping outline to mean shape

messages.author: 4c2b8549469e242c
messages.subject: Trouble warping outline to mean shape
parts:
Dear all,

I have a question about the WarpRefOutline fuction. I've been trying to warp the outline of the closest to average specimen to a mean specimen computed with mshape but I'm not managing and I think there is something that I keep missing when I read the guide.

I have a sample of 17 aligned specimens with 10 fixed landmarks. I have obtained the estimated mean shape for my aligned specimens using mshape, and then I used findMeanSpec to find the specimen which is the closest to the average. I have obtained an outline for this (original-non aligned) specimen and extracted xy coordinates using ImageJ. Then I have digitised a fake specimen using this outline and saved the coordinates as a tps file to be used as the "coord" argument.
I converted the fixed landmark data for the close-to-average specimen into a 2D matrix.
The outline and landmarks read fine, but when I run WarpRefOutline, I get this error message: 

Error in matr - matrix(M[i, ], p, 2, byrow = TRUE) : 
  non-numeric argument to binary operator

I'm not quite sure why this is happening so I was hoping someone might spot the mistake I'm missing!

Here is my code:


XXGPA=gpagen(X,ProcD = F)
aligned_specimens=XXGPA$coords

meanshape=mshape(aligned_specimens)

findMeanSpec(aligned_specimens)

outline=read.table("test_outline.txt")

meanfixes=readland.tps("MeanSpec_digit.tps")
mat_meanfixes=matrix(meanfixes,ncol=2,nrow=10)

warpRefOutline(outline,mat_meanfixes,meanshape)



Many thanks in advance!

Lou

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: Trouble warping outline to mean shape
parts:
Very simple fix here. When you read in the "MeanSpec.tps" file using readland.tps, the output is a 3D array. Since you need only the matrix of coordinates of that single specimen, then take that specimen from the 3D array using indexing, like:

meanfixes=readland.tps("MeanSpec_digit.tps")

warpRefOutline(outline,mat_meanfixes[,,1],meanshape) # here using [,,1] takes the first specimen (and only specimen of 
meanfixes)

mat_meanfixes=matrix(meanfixes,ncol=2,nrow=10) # was not correct, and was misaligning your data.

Emma

messages.subject: Re: Trouble warping outline to mean shape
parts:
Hi Emma,

Many thanks for your answer, please excuse me for the late reply.
I'm afraid I'm still getting the same error message with "warpRefOutline(outline,meanfixes[,,1],meanshape)"

I do get a plot of the imported outline with landmarks, but I can't get the warping part right (Error in matr - matrix(M[i, ], p, 2, byrow = TRUE) :
non-numeric argument to binary operator).

Could this by any chance be because the "coord" and the "ref" aren't in the same orientation? Both are left profiles but one is facing down whereas the other is facing left. I tried to warp them after a procrustes alignement just to see if this could be the issue, but then of course the outline and its "coord" file didn't correspond anymore.

Thanks again for your help, 

Lou

messages.author: 91722721526eb1d7
messages.subject: Re: Trouble warping outline to mean shape
parts:
Hi Lou,

Everything must be in the same coordinate space and same orientation. That is, if you plot the outline, and the mat_meanfixes[,,1], they will perfectly align. 

Also, make sure that all elements are numerical! check with is.numeric()

Emma
